tasks.subject: [community-administration-contract] [P1] Add settings, lifecycle, host audit, and deletion-job schema
tasks.description:
Consume DOR-2172's pre-second-tenant blob inventory/reservation and legacy reconciliation foundation. Extend it with validated settings, lifecycle version/timestamps, suspended resume state, tenant-qualified icon purpose, host lifecycle audit, deletion jobs, per-blob lifecycle deletion progress, and content-free expiring tombstones. Preserve DOR-2171's owner and host-operator invariants.

Acceptance criteria:
- DOR-2172 has already assigned or drained every legacy managed object and blocks second-community creation if storage ownership is incomplete.
- The database constrains every state/resume-state combination and one live owner where required.
- Settings and lifecycle versions support compare-and-swap mutations.
- New icon objects use the same immutable tenant ownership established for attachments and exports before bytes are stored.
- Deletion progress keys every row by immutable community UUID and cannot reference another tenant's blob.
- Tombstone columns cannot retain names, account/member IDs, content, blob keys, or credentials.
- Existing single-community data migrates to active, invite-only settings without ID drift.

tasks.subject: [community-administration-contract] [P1] Implement host metadata, creation, claims, and abandonment
tasks.description:
Add host-operator routes that list metadata-only community projections, create idempotent pending-owner tenants, issue/revoke 24-hour tenant-bound claims, and abandon only empty unclaimed tenants. Keep claim secrets on the private no-store handoff.

Acceptance criteria:
- Host-only operators cannot read any member directory, channel, entry, file, export, or tenant audit content.
- Retrying one creation key returns the same tenant; changed payload returns 409.
- Claim redemption atomically creates the sole owner and activates the tenant.
- Claims cannot target any non-pending state.
- Abandonment proves no membership/content exists and cannot affect first-install bootstrap or another tenant.

tasks.subject: [community-administration-contract] [P1] Implement versioned settings and private icons
tasks.description:
Add strict tenant settings DTOs and ETag mutations. Owner controls name/admission; owner and admin control description/icon. Store bounded raster icons through BlobStore, proxy authorized reads, and queue replaced blobs for exact deletion. Apply the same tenant-qualified reservation protocol to icons, attachments, and exports: reserve before storage, then re-lock and recheck tenant lifecycle/version when committing the reference. Closing admission revokes outstanding invitations and pending admissions in the same transaction.

Acceptance criteria:
- Stale If-Match fails without overwriting a concurrent update.
- Names remain display-only and cannot alter canonical routing.
- Icon upload rejects external URLs, SVG, oversized and unsupported bytes; no storage URL escapes.
- Old icons are reclaimed only after the new reference commits.
- An upload racing archive/suspend/delete cannot commit a reference and remains attributable to that tenant for cleanup.
- Role-negative and cross-tenant cases produce no mutation.

tasks.subject: [community-administration-contract] [P1] Enforce transfer, archive, restore, suspension, and immediate revocation
tasks.description:
Make lifecycle transitions use recent reauthentication, ETags, tenant locks, exact role checks, audit, typed unavailable responses, and immediate stream/credential revocation. Transfer remains active-only and changes the former owner to member. Restore/resume never revives a grant, invitation, agent, or credential.

Acceptance criteria:
- Transfer races leave exactly one owner and never cross tenants.
- Archive preserves every content row/blob while ending writes, invitations, pairings, grants, agents, and streams.
- Owner export/restore/delete remain available while archived; ordinary content is read-only.
- Suspension rejects every tenant credential and resumes to the recorded active/archive state.
- Host authority alone cannot transfer, archive, restore, or read content.

tasks.subject: [community-administration-contract] [P1] Implement cancelable owner deletion requests
tasks.description:
Add owner-only deletion request/cancel routes with recent reauthentication, ETag, exact name plus UUID-suffix confirmation, seven-day grace, immediate revocation, idempotency, and server-reported status. Offer but do not require a fresh export. Cancel returns to archived and keeps credentials revoked.

Acceptance criteria:
- Active and archived owners can request; other roles/states cannot.
- The worker cannot run before delete_after.
- Retry returns the same job without extending the deadline.
- Cancel works only before the deadline for the same still-active owner membership.
- The UI/API never describes an owner export as a disaster-recovery backup.

tasks.subject: [community-administration-contract] [P1] Build bounded exact-tenant deletion and tombstone expiry
tasks.description:
Implement a SKIP-LOCKED bounded worker that deletes every object in the tenant-qualified inventory, including current icons/attachments/exports, outstanding upload reservations, replaced objects, and failed unreferenced-object cleanup, before removing tenant rows. Record per-key retry progress, then write and expire the redacted host tombstone. Keep failure status observable without secret/raw provider errors.

Acceptance criteria:
- Injected object and database failures resume from committed progress without skipping or double-counting work.
- Tenant rows are retained until all references, reservations, cleanup rows, and managed objects owned by that tenant are confirmed absent.
- The worker cannot report completion while an A object remains after bytes were stored but its metadata transaction failed.
- A deletion job for A cannot select or delete a B row/blob, including caller-tampered IDs.
- Host-wide accounts, sessions, OAuth records, and host operators survive.
- Completed tombstones contain only allowed fields and disappear after 30 days.

tasks.subject: [community-administration-contract] [P2] Build host and community settings surfaces
tasks.description:
Build metadata-only host administration and contextual community Settings sections for Presentation, Access, People, Export, and Danger Zone. Render controls from server-confirmed authority, show immutable short IDs beside destructive actions, and reconcile ETag conflicts without discarding edits.

Acceptance criteria:
- Host-only operators see no tenant content or private member data.
- Owner/admin/member controls match the authority matrix.
- Create/claim, settings, icon, transfer, archive/restore, suspension, and status errors have loading/empty/retry states.
- Names never replace IDs in requests or cache keys.
- The surface works by keyboard and at narrow phone width.

tasks.subject: [community-administration-contract] [P2] Build durable destructive-action and deletion progress UX
tasks.description:
Implement reauthentication and identity confirmations, reload-safe deletion countdown/progress, cancel behavior, partial cleanup errors, and post-lifecycle routing. Archived members remain on a read-only canonical community surface with owner restore/export/delete controls; removed, suspended, or deleting people move to another membership or the chooser without host sign-out.

Acceptance criteria:
- Dialog copy names the community and consequences and traps/restores focus correctly.
- Archived history stays readable, and the owner's allowed archived controls stay reachable.
- Deletion cannot submit without both required confirmations and a current server version.
- Reload obtains status from the server rather than client timers or optimistic memory.
- Cleanup failures show a safe retrying state, not a false success.
- Archive/delete are distinct and export is offered without blocking deletion.

tasks.subject: [community-administration-contract] [P3] Prove the administration permission and concurrency matrix
tasks.description:
Run API and browser coverage for every authority row, stale settings writes, transfer/lifecycle races, two browser profiles, state-specific routes, stream termination, credential revocation, accessible dialogs, and mobile layout.

Acceptance criteria:
- Every positive role path has a negative host-only/admin/member/cross-tenant counterpart.
- Races preserve the owner and lifecycle invariants.
- Archive/restore and suspend/resume preserve exact content while keeping old machine credentials revoked.
- Browser assertions observe redirects, errors, focus, and server-confirmed progress.
- Cloud egress can be blocked without breaking administration.

tasks.subject: [community-administration-contract] [P3] Prove exact deletion, retry, and unaffected-tenant recovery
tasks.description:
With tenants A and B, exercise deletion cancel, early-worker refusal, object/database failure injection, restart/retry, exact final row/blob removal, tombstone minimization/expiry, and host-wide identity preservation. Include stored-but-uncommitted A uploads, replaced icons awaiting cleanup, and uploads racing the lifecycle transition. Rehearse host backup restore separately to show it is not selective online tenant recovery.

Acceptance criteria:
- Before/after manifests prove every A row/blob, reservation, and pending cleanup is removed and every B row/blob/session/stream is unchanged.
- An orphaned A object blocks completion until it is deleted; a racing upload cannot escape tenant ownership or commit after the lifecycle change.
- Interrupted cleanup resumes exactly and reports honest status.
- No deleted tenant content or personal identifier remains in operational tables/logs.
- Accounts with B membership stay signed in and usable.
- Evidence distinguishes owner export from coordinated host disaster recovery.
